successCriteria.description: The `Balance` entity interface is defined and importable from `src/modules/balance/balance.model.ts` with all canonical fields: id, employeeId, leaveType, totalEntitlement, usedDays, remainingDays, fiscalYear, status (typed as BalanceStatus), createdAt, updatedAt

The `IBalanceRepository` interface is defined with all six methods: findByEmployeeId, findByEmployeeIdAndLeaveType, findByEmployeeIdAndFiscalYear, create, update, deductDays — each with the correct parameter and return types matching the PLAN.md specification

The `IBalanceService` interface is defined with three methods: getBalance(employeeId, leaveType), hasSufficientBalance(employeeId, leaveType, requestedDays), deductBalance(employeeId, leaveType, days) — each with correct signatures
Domain error classes `InsufficientBalanceError` (code: 'INSUFFICIENT_BALANCE') and `BalanceNotFoundError` (code: 'NOT_FOUND') are defined and exportable from the balance module

The `AuditLog` entity interface is defined and importable from `src/modules/audit-log/audit-log.model.ts` with all canonical fields: id, entityType, entityId, action, performedBy, changes (Record<string, unknown>), createdAt (Date)
The `IAuditLogRepository` interface is defined with three methods: findByEntity(entityType, entityId), create(entry), findAll(filters?) — each with correct parameter and return types
The `AuditLogValidationError` class (code: 'VALIDATION_ERROR') is defined and exportable from the audit-log module
TypeScript compilation succeeds with `tsc --noEmit` — all interface files are valid TypeScript with no type errors, no use of `any`, and strict null checks pass

constraints: No concrete implementations — this phase produces only TypeScript interfaces, entity types, and error classes. No repository classes, no service classes, no database queries, no HTTP routes, no controllers
The `Balance` entity's `status` field must be typed as `BalanceStatus` (imported from `src/shared/types`), not as a plain string
The `AuditLog.changes` field must be typed as `Record<string, unknown>`, not `any` — per the HARNESS.json `no-any` constraint
Error classes must extend `Error` and expose a `code` property (string literal) for HTTP mapping — matching the pattern established by existing error classes in the codebase
Repository interfaces must return `Promise<T>` for all methods — all data access is asynchronous (PostgreSQL-backed)
outOfScope: Concrete repository implementations (PgBalanceRepository, PgAuditLogRepository) — deferred to Phase 4 (part 2/2)
Concrete service implementation (BalanceService) — deferred to Phase 4 (part 2/2)
